messages:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: High p99 response latency and memory pressure observed on serving-pool-7 for model: redwood/giga-3. Trigger: latency spike + host OOMs at 2026-02-14 22:10:00 UTC
incidents-bot: Summary: sustained token-latency > 1.8s p95, API errors 500 (OOM) rising from 0.2% -> 6% in 10m; autoscaler triggered restarts.
alice-runtime: ACK, I'm on it. Oncall routing shows continuous-batching queue depth jumped ~5x.
ben-oncall: grabbing logs now. Observed large KV cache sizes on the same hosts.
ben-oncall: tail of worker logs:
```
[2026-02-14T22:08:42Z] worker: batch started seqs=28 tokens=5120 model=giga-3
[2026-02-14T22:08:42Z] kvcache: insert prefix_size=4096 total_cached_tokens=1.3e6
[2026-02-14T22:08:43Z] mem: RSS 31GB -> 62GB OOM risk
```
carmen-sre: 28 seqs? our max_num_seqs is supposed to be 8 in prod. Did a config flip happen?
dave-eng: We rolled a batching profile yesterday for internal perf tests. I asked infra for a canary but looks like the canary flag got flipped to prod by mistake (config key: `continuous_batch.profile=stress-high`).
alice-runtime: That profile sets `max_num_seqs=32` and `max_batch_tokens=8192` to maximize throughput in bench. That's likely why KV cache exploded (prefixes kept for many sequences) and we started retaining huge KV.
eva-cust-success: Heads-up: customer AcmeApp reported degraded latency in webapp at ~22:09 UTC. They're seeing timeouts.
ben-oncall: Immediate mitigation plan: revert profile -> set `continuous_batch.profile=balanced` and force per-worker soft-eviction of KV caches, plus limit max_num_seqs=8. I'll run hotfix script.
ben-oncall: Running hotfix:
```bash
# hotfix: revert batching profile + set conservative caps
kubectl set env deployment/serving-pool-7 continuous_batch.profile=balanced -n redwood-serving
kubectl exec -it worker-7a -- /bin/sh -c 'echo 1 > /proc/sys/kvm/evict_kvcache' || true
```
alice-runtime: Also change runtime config temporarily: `max_batch_tokens=2048`, `max_num_seqs=6`, `batch_timeout_ms=30` to prioritize latency.
dave-eng: Pushing config change to config-service (vaulted):
```json
{
  "continuous_batch": {
    "max_num_seqs": 6,
    "max_batch_tokens": 2048,
    "batch_timeout_ms": 30
  }
}
```
ops-bot: Deploy ticket created: #INC-6219, runbook step 'revert-profile' executed by ben-oncall.
ben-oncall: Applying rollout now (canary=0.1 -> 0.5 -> 1.0):
- set env on deployment (done)
- restart pods rolling (in progress)
- monitor mem & p99
carmen-sre: Watching metrics. After first 10 pods rolled: p95 latency dropped from 1.8s -> 450ms; mem usage back down to 26-28GB. Error rate falling.
eva-cust-success: Updated AcmeApp with status: we have identified a batching config regression and are rolling a fix; ETA 15-20m. They replied thanks but asked for postmortem and whether any data leaked.
alice-runtime: No evidence of data exfil. KV cache contents are transient model keys (prefix tokens). We will rotate audit logs and double-check.
dave-eng: We should add a guard in config-service to block profiles that set max_num_seqs > 16 in prod unless an explicit override flag is used.
ben-oncall: Rollout completed at 22:25 UTC, all pods healthy. p99 now 320ms, errors at baseline. Continuing observation.
ops-bot: Incident severity set to P2 due to customer impact and partial outages. Paging paused.
ben-oncall: Handing off to carmen for overnight watch in 30m. Carmen, can you take over?
carmen-sre: Taking it. I'll keep an eye on evictions and autoscaler churn overnight. Also create follow-up ticket to audit recent config changes and map ACLs to who can flip profiles.
ben-oncall: Created follow-up: ENGOPS-4821 (audit profiles + runbook update). Assigning to dave-eng for corrective change.
dave-eng: On it. Will add config guard and a canary gate that requires explicit 'canary=true' when flipping high-throughput profiles.
eva-cust-success: AcmeApp notified that fix deployed; they acknowledged improvement and will monitor on their side.
alice-runtime: Postmortem owners: dave-eng (cause & config guard), carmen-sre (mitigation & runbook), ben-oncall (hotfix timeline). Draft due in 72h.
carmen-sre: Note for postmortem: root cause: human-triggered profile flip exposed a lab profile into prod. Contributing factor: no approval gate and no max cap sensor on continuous-batch config. Impact: multiple customer requests timed out, autoscaler restarts increased 3x, transient OOMs on 4 hosts.
ben-oncall: Closing out immediate incident thread; will link to postmortem when available. Adding a note: if we see KV cache growth > 500k tokens in 5m window, trigger auto-limiter to set `max_num_seqs=8` until operator clears.
incidents-bot: Incident resolved: upgraded to mitigated at 2026-02-14 22:40:00 UTC.
